newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Bindley Western sees more acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Bindley Western sees more acquisitions.

text.p: Drug wholesaler Bindley Western Industries Inc continues on the acquisition trail, looking to add new products or geographic areas.
Last week, Indianapolis-based Bindley Western acquired Tennessee Wholesale Drug Co, which had sales of $308 million in the fiscal year ended March 31, for an undisclosed amount of cash.

"I can't say that we would have any that would be exactly like that, but I anticipate that we will have additional acquisitions, maybe over on the Priority Healthcare side of the business," Bindley Western chairman and chief executive William Bindley said in an interview Tuesday.
Priority Healthcare is a specialty pharmaceutical provider to oncology offices, dialysis clinics and the office-based physician market.

Bindley Western has previously announced plans to split Priority off into a stand alone company and that move is "very close," Bindley said. The exact form of the split-off has yet to be decided, but it could include a partial spin-off, with Bindley Western owning enough of a stake to report consolidated results, he said.
In terms of acquisitions for the unit, Bindley Western is looking to either add a product line, or to add to its geographic reach.
"What we would look for is a product line we are not in, or a strong geographic presence," Bindley said.

Geographically, the company is strong on the Eastern Seaboard, Florida, parts of the Midwest, the Southwest and Southern California. Bindley Western is also setting up distribution operations in Sacramento, California and Portland, Oregon.
The company is also looking to expand its operations into the Plains states and the upper Midwest in 1998, through acquisition or de novo operations.
"We would look at either," Bindley said. "If we don't or cannot find an acquisition that makes sense from all our criteria...we would open from scratch."

In terms of the Tennessee Wholesale deal, Bindley Western noted that about 90 percent of Tennessee Wholesale's revenues came from managed care customers, fitting in with Bindley Western's goal of increasing its market share in that business.

Bindley said he expects about a third of the company's wholesale drug revenues to come from managed care by the end of the year, while a third will come from drugstore chains and a third will come from independent pharmacies.
"Going forward, managed care is going to grow faster, certainly than independent pahrmacies, because the universe of managed care is growing quicker," he said.
Bindley Western shares were up 5/16 at 23-11/16 Wednesday.
